cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to the prophet Ezekiel, and this time it's aimed at one of Israel's neighbors. God says, 'Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.' That's not a glance, friend, that's the FULL stare-down.

cards.question: God gives the Ammonites a reason. It goes back to the day His sanctuary was profaned, Israel's land was laid waste and Judah went into exile. What did the Ammonites do that day?

cards.text: So God will give the Ammonites to the people of the East, who will pitch their tents among them and eat their fruit and drink their milk. Cheer at your neighbor's bad day, and SUDDENLY there are strangers camping in YOUR yard.

cards.question: God says He'll make the Ammonite city of Rabbah a pasture for camels. What does that picture tell you about Rabbah?

answers.text: It will become grazing land for animals
It will become a busy trading city
It will become a strong fortress

cards.question: True or false: God says that when all this happens to them, the Ammonites will know that He is the LORD.

cards.text: Then God gives a second reason: the Ammonites clapped their hands and stomped their feet over the land of Israel. Clapping AND stomping? Friend, that's not a reaction, that's a halftime show.

cards.question: God says the Ammonites rejoiced over the land of Israel with a heart full of ___.

cards.text: So God will stretch out His hand against the Ammonites and give them as plunder to the nations. Halftime's over, friend.

cards.question: True or false: God says He'll take some of Ammon's land but leave the Ammonites themselves alone.

cards.text: Next up is Moab, and with it Seir, the area where Esau settled (Genesis 36:8). They had something to say about the house of Judah too.

cards.question: Moab and Seir looked at what happened to the house of Judah. What did they say about it?

answers.text: Judah is like all the other nations
Judah will rise again very soon
Judah has no friends left anywhere

cards.question: True or false: When God exposes the flank of Moab, He starts with its frontier cities, the ones He calls the glory of the land.
God gives Moab, along with the Ammonites, to the people of the East. What does He say will happen to the Ammonites among the nations?

answers.text: They will no longer be remembered
They will be honored once again
They will rule over all of them

cards.text: So God will execute judgments on Moab, and they will know that He is the LORD. Moab looked at Judah and said, 'Eh, just regular,' and God heard EVERY word.
Now God turns to Edom, the nation that came from Esau (Genesis 36:1). God says Edom acted vengefully against the house of Judah.

cards.question: True or false: God says that by acting vengefully against Judah, Edom incurred grievous guilt.

cards.text: God will make Edom a wasteland, and from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword. Teman to Dedan? That's not a neighborhood, friend, that's the WHOLE map.

cards.question: God says He'll take His vengeance on Edom. Whose hand will He use to do it?
True or false: God says Israel will deal with Edom according to Israel's own anger.

cards.text: Last come the Philistines. Yes, friend, Goliath's people (1 Samuel 17:4).

cards.question: God says the Philistines took vengeance with malice of soul, trying to destroy Judah with ___ hostility.

cards.text: So God says, 'Behold, I will stretch out My hand against the Philistines.' He'll destroy the remnant along the coast, and there's one more name on that list.

cards.question: Along with the remnant on the coast, who does God say He'll cut off?
How does God describe what He'll execute against the Philistines?

answers.text: A quiet warning to turn back

cards.text: Then they will know that He is the LORD, when He lays His vengeance upon them. Five 'becauses,' five 'therefores,' and I counted them all on my mustache, friend.
